title: 8 Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them
use_cases: Use when balancing internal monologue with external action to avoid redundancy
Implement when switching between close, distant, and omniscient perspectives
Configure when establishing explicit transitions between character points of view
Use when auditing a manuscript for tone consistency and narrative immersion
Implement when selecting the most effective focalization for a character's development
content:
| Pitfall | Why It Happens | Remedy | Over‑exposure of Internal Thoughts | Over‑use of first‑person leads to redundancy. | Balance with external scenes, use dialogue. | Unclear POV Shifts | Sudden changes confuse readers. | Signpost shifts explicitly (e.g., “From now on…”). | Inconsistent Voice | Mixing tones breaks immersion. | Maintain a consistent narrator voice throughout. |

1. Rewrite a Scene in Three Distances – close, distant, and omniscient.
2. Create a Character Profile with Focalization Choices– decide which POV best suits the character’s arc.
